expectations.text: Identifies that during the rollout window old code runs against the new schema
expectations.evidence: for some window, old pods/instances still running the previous code will issue `SELECT ... legacy_email` against a table where the column no longer exists. Every one of those queries errors

expectations.text: Recommends splitting into separate deploys (expand/contract) rather than shipping the drop with the code
expectations.evidence: This is textbook expand/contract — you're at the *contract* step, which is the one that gets its own deploy: [Deploy A: code changes] [Deploy B: next week DROP COLUMN]

expectations.text: States that dropping the column is irreversible without a backup or restore
expectations.evidence: Once it runs, the data in that column is gone — a code revert does not bring it back. What restores it is a database backup taken *before* the migration, and only one that someone has actually restored from

expectations.text: Addresses what rollback looks like if the deploy goes wrong
expectations.evidence: Deploy A rolls back in the time it takes to redeploy the previous image. Deploy B rolls back via a restore, which is hours and needs the people who know the restore procedure

expectations.text: Addresses the Friday timing in terms of who is available to respond, not as superstition
expectations.evidence: The Friday question is really: is the restore path staffed this afternoon and over the weekend?

expectations.text: Recommends a CI gate that blocks destructive DDL from landing alongside application code
expectations.evidence: fail any PR whose changed migrations contain `DROP`... unless it carries an explicit `destructive-migration` label — and reject the label on PRs that also touch application code, which mechanically enforces the split

expectations.text: Does not approve the merge as-is on the strength of green CI
expectations.evidence: CI green is true but irrelevant to the two actual risks

expectations.text: Distinguishes the reversible parts of the change from the irreversible part
expectations.evidence: Deploy A rolls back in the time it takes to redeploy... Deploy B rolls back via a restore
